It looks like the NTLM_REMOTE_SUPPLEMENTAL_CREDENTIAL struct in MS-CSSP appendix <22> Section 2.2.1.2.3.1 is wrong, and the MSV1_0_CREDENTIAL_KEY comes before the MSV1_0_CREDENTIAL_KEY_TYPE. I'll ping MS dochelp and refer to here.

CC: @hardening1 FYI
MS dochelp have confirmed that, see: https://lists.samba.org/archive/cifs-protocol/2021-June/003600.html
Attached packet capture and keys (packet 460): [TSRemoteGuardCreds.tgz](/uploads/5745e505561d8bfce39c98df6841d20e/TSRemoteGuardCreds.tgz)

Hi @AndersBroman, this is ready for review from my end, no test commits lurking.. thanks!
@iboukris just curious, do you have any plan to add decoding for MICs ?
Hi @hardening1, I don't have much of a plan really, just investigating the protocol and dissecting what I can figure out, but what MICs are you referring to? Is it in the credssp part?
yes
Where? could you refer to the doc or to a packet from the attached capture? I can see the spnego mechListMIC but it doesn't seem to need further dissection.

Looking at krb5 implementation (https://github.com/krb5/krb5/blob/master/src/lib/gssapi/krb5/k5unseal.c#L363) it looks like the MICs have their own format (although I can't find where it's documented)

Not sure but it looks like the 'krb5_sgn_cksum' part of the gss_wrap/unwrap blobs, which is already dissected by the kerberos code, for instance in packet 460 in the attached capture:
```
krb5_blob: 050406ff0000001c0000000076f0d578456549057cf5b12b9a3f32fe3b140b8d1d10dc8d…
    krb5_tok_id: KRB_TOKEN_CFX_WRAP (0x0405)
    krb5_cfx_flags: 0x06, AcceptorSubkey, Sealed
        .... .1.. = AcceptorSubkey: Set
        .... ..1. = Sealed: Set
        .... ...0 = SendByAcceptor: Not set
    krb5_filler: ff
    krb5_cfx_ec: 0
    krb5_cfx_rrc: 28
    krb5_cfx_seq: 1995494776
    krb5_sgn_cksum: 456549057cf5b12b9a3f32fe3b140b8d1d10dc8da4716b9291c9307a3baf2023173f3055…
Ok found the doc here: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4121#page-12 and you're right applying the `spnego-krb5` dissector on mechList shall dissect it correctly and expose a MIC token.
https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/3525 seems to do the job for the MIC field
